population.unit: one row per distinct server name, classified on its isLatest=true version

method.remote_check: for each remotes[].url: DNS via getaddrinfo(host,443); if it resolves, one HEAD (GET on 405/error) with 10s timeout. alive = any HTTP status received.
method.package_check: npm: GET https://registry.npmjs.org/<identifier>/<version>; pypi: GET https://pypi.org/pypi/<identifier>/<version>/json. 200=OK, 404=MISSING, else UNCHECKABLE.
method.politeness: 0.2s sleep between network calls; DNS and package lookups cached per key
method.state_rule: <remote_state>_<package_state>; UNCHECKABLE if any package lookup was neither 200 nor 404. REMOTE_ALIVE_PACKAGE_OK is an extra state the brief did not list; it is reported rather than folded into a listed one.

pypi_mcp_name_marker_check.note: the registry's PyPI ownership gate looks for 'mcp-name: <registry name>' in the package description; all 39 dead-remote packages carry it, so a corrective publish would pass that gate

corrections_to_brief: The brief said every remotes[] URL points at api.meok.ai. On isLatest versions 39 of 40 do; 1 (io.github.CSOAI-ORG/gspc 1.4.2) points at https://councilof.ai/mcp, which resolves and answered HTTP 200.
The brief's five-state vocabulary has no slot for a live remote; a sixth state REMOTE_ALIVE_PACKAGE_OK is added rather than misfiling the row.
honesty: self-published listings show distribution, not adoption
limitations: Only the isLatest version of each name is classified; 988 older versions are counted but not checked.
A remote that resolves and returns any HTTP status is called alive; no MCP handshake was attempted.
The registry search endpoint was trusted to return the full namespace; it was cross-checked against the full walk in x1-mcp-publisher-concentration-2026-09-22.json where that walk completed.
Package OK means the exact version exists on the package registry today; it says nothing about whether it installs or runs.

redactions.rule: tokens carrying an internal codename or a retracted claim word are replaced by withheld-by-brand-gate:<sha256[:12] of the token>; the registry itself still serves the names; counts are unaffected
